figures.caption: TABLE III: RQ1 configuration sweep on HumanEval; columns and conventions as in Table II. All numbers are percentages.

TABLE II: RQ1 configuration sweep on BigCodeBench. Per-model AccVal (mean and std-dev (subscript) over folds) for every construction method (pca/mean-diff (md)), read-out location (last token (last)/response average (avg)), fitting framing, and validation=testing framing (neut/conc/func). First row ≈ prior work [11]; directions fit in- or out-of-distribution (MBPP+/synthetic); per-column maxima in bold. All numbers are percentages.
TABLE IV: ANOVA for RQ1. η2 = variance share in AccVal from a factor (main effect) or an interaction. Panels (1)–(4) follow Sections IV-1–IV-4

TABLE VII: Per-model view of the confound check: AccVal for a mean-diff direction fit on a benchmark’s controlled pairs without the rewrites (MOnly) and with them (MC), followed by the change in percentage points (∆ = MC − M-Only). Settings follow Table V (weighted sampling, averaged over read-out locations and framings), and the All column reproduces its model-averaged cells. Two kinds of row support no conclusion and are marked accordingly: † scores each variant on its own held-out pairs, so the two accuracies come from different test sets; ‡ leaves every model near the 25% chance level of the 1-of-4 selection, so neither variant transfers there. The four unmarked rows share a test set and reach 60.7%, and carry the comparison.

TABLE V: RQ2 transfer: mean-diff direction fit on a benchmark’s controlled pairs (M-Only/MC), test on BigCodeBench, HumanEval, and held-out split of those pairs. Cells are AccVal (best layer in parentheses), averaged over read-out locations, framings, and models. Top block is RQ1’s mean-diff on the same test sets, differs only in fitting source. Dashes mark conditions not run; † fits on one benchmark, tests on the other.
